```{r, include = FALSE}
tract <- read_csv("tract_cbsa.csv") %>% 
  mutate(dens_mult = dens*1000000)

# Long format race data
race_long <- tract %>%
  select(pct_white, pct_black, pct_asian, pct_hispanic, pm25) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct"),
    names_to = "race",
    values_to = "percent") %>% 
  mutate(race = case_when(race == "pct_white" ~ "White",
                          race == "pct_black" ~ "Black",
```

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

# Fixing names
state_lookup <- tibble(
  state_abb = state.abb,
  region = tolower(state.name))

# State means
state_summary <- tract %>%
  group_by(state_abb) %>%
  summarise(mean_pm = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  left_join(state_lookup, by = "state_abb")

states_map <- map_data("state")
map_df <- states_map %>%
  left_join(state_summary, by = "region")

map_1 <- ggplot(map_df, aes(long, lat, group = group, fill = mean_pm)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +

  tract %>%
  group_by(state_abb) %>%
  summarise(
    total_pop = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE),
```

# Modeling
## Approach 1: Nested LMM
```{r}
nested_mod <- lmerTest::lmer(pm25 ~ pct_white*pct_pov 
                             + ruca_agg + log(dens_mult) + (1 | state_abb/cbsa_id),
                     data = tract)

nested_mod |> 
  broom.mixed::glance() |> 
  knitr::kable(booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE)  |> 
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 12)
```

<!-- $$ -->
<!-- \begin{aligned} -->
<!-- &\ Y_{ijk} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{PCT_WHITE} + \beta_2 \text{PCT_POV} + \beta_{3} \text{(Area = Suburban)} +\\ -->
<!-- &\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \  \beta_{3} \text{(Area = Urban)} + \beta_4 \text{log(Density)} + \beta_5 \text{(PCT_WHITE x PCT_POV)} + b_{j(k)}{CSBA(State)},\\ -->
<!-- &\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \  i = 1, .., 58030, j = 1, ...., 380, k = 1,..., 47 -->
<!-- \end{aligned} -->
<!-- $$ -->

```{r}
tbl_regression(
  nested_mod,
  intercept = TRUE,
  estimate_fun = function(x) {
    ifelse(abs(x) < 0.001,
           formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 2),
           formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3))
  }) |> 
  bold_p() |> 
  bold_labels() |> 
  as_gt() |> 
  tab_options(latex.tbl.pos = "h")
```

Note for Interpretation: per 10% increase

Checking random effects too
```{r, fig.height=4}
re <- ranef(nested_mod, condVar = TRUE)

# Example: CBSA intercepts (nested in state)
cbsa_re <- re$`cbsa_id:state_abb`  # random intercepts for CBSAs

cbsa_re <- cbsa_re %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "cbsa_id") %>%
  rename(random_intercept = `(Intercept)`)

ggplot(cbsa_re, aes(x = random_intercept)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Random Intercepts (CBSAs)",
       x = "Random Intercept (Deviation from Overall Intercept)",
       y = "Count")
```

CBSA RI within each state
```{r, fig.height=4}
re_cbsa <- ranef(nested_mod, condVar = TRUE)$`cbsa_id:state_abb`
re_sd <- attr(re_cbsa, "postVar")[1,,] |> sqrt()  # standard deviation for intercept

cbsa_re <- tibble(
  cbsa_id = rownames(re_cbsa),
  random_intercept = re_cbsa$`(Intercept)`,
  sd = re_sd
)

ggplot(cbsa_re, aes(x = reorder(cbsa_id, random_intercept), y = random_intercept)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = random_intercept - 1.96*sd,
                    ymax = random_intercept + 1.96*sd), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Intercepts with 95% CI (CBSA)",
       x = "CBSA",
       y = "Random Intercept") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
  axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

State-level RI
```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
state_re <- ranef(nested_mod)$state_abb %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "state_abb") %>%
  rename(random_intercept = `(Intercept)`)

ggplot(state_re, aes(x = reorder(state_abb, random_intercept), y = random_intercept)) +

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Intercepts by State",
```

## Approach 2: Cross classified Multilevel modeling (CCMM)
```{r}
############################# Data assessment ###########################

cbsa_data  <- tract %>% mutate(state_fips = factor(state_fips),
state_abb = factor(state_abb) ,
county_fips = factor(county_fips),
geoid = factor(geoid)    ,
cbsa_id = factor(cbsa_id)   ,
#ruca = factor(ruca)     ,
ruca_agg = factor(ruca_agg),
density_log = log(dens_mult))


## Check the distinct count of states, cbsa, census tracts and county

n_distinct(cbsa_data$state_abb) ## No Massachusetts, Wyoming
n_distinct(cbsa_data$cbsa_id)
n_distinct(cbsa_data$county_fips)
n_distinct(cbsa_data$geoid)

## Check for missingness in outcome

sum(is.na(cbsa_data$pm25)) # 1 missing

## Check the distribution of outcome

hist(cbsa_data$pm25) ## normal data


## Check whether data is actually nested or cross classified

### 1. Does each tract belong to one CBSA?

cbsa_data %>%
  group_by(geoid) %>%
  summarise(n_cbsa = n_distinct(cbsa_id)) %>%
  filter(n_cbsa > 1) ## Truly nested

### 2. Does each CBSA belong to only ONE state
cbsa_data %>%
  group_by(cbsa_id) %>%
  summarise(n_states = n_distinct(state_fips)) %>%
  filter(n_states > 1) ## 43 cbsa_ids appear in more than 1 state; not truly nested


### Plot to show non-nested CBSAs
cbsa_data %>%
  group_by(cbsa_id) %>%
  summarise(n_states = factor(n_distinct(state_fips))) %>% ggplot(aes(n_states)) + geom_bar() + labs(
    #title = "Count of CBSA ",
    x = "Number of states",        # x-axis label
    y = "CBSA count"    # y-axis label
  ) + theme_minimal() + scale_fill_viridis_d()



  labs(
    title = "Example Bar Plot",
    x = "Category",        # x-axis label
    y = "Count / Value"    # y-axis label
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


## Check correlations and multicolinearity

### Correlation
#cor(cbsa_data[, c("pct_white","pct_hispanic","pct_black", "pct_pov", "dens_mult", "bc", "pm25", "ruca", "hyads")], use = "complete.obs")


### Multicolinearity using non-nested model

#vif(lm(pm25 ~ pct_white + pct_hispanic + pct_black + pct_pov + ruca_agg + dens + bc + hyads, data = cbsa_data))

```


```{r fig.height=15, fig.width=10,  fig.align='left'}

# Justification:

# Each tract belongs to one CBSA
# Each tract belongs to one state
# But CBSAs and states are not truly nested within each other i.e., cbsa crosses state boundaries
      ## So tracts are simultaneously classified by:
            ## Tract ∈ CBSA
            ## Tract ∈ State
# Can compute between cbsa and state variances as well as within tract variances

# Limitations:

## Assumes normal random effects
## It doesn't handle spatial autocorrelation
## If state doesn't contribute any variance it becomes an unneccessarily model complex with no benefit


## Nested LMM 
cc_model1 <- lmer(
  pm25 ~ pct_white*pct_pov  + ruca_agg + density_log + 
    #(1 | cbsa_id) +
    (1 | state_abb/cbsa_id),
  data = cbsa_data
)


## CCMM
cc_model <- lmer(
  pm25 ~ pct_white*pct_pov +  ruca_agg + density_log + 
    (1 | cbsa_id) +
    (1 | state_abb),
  data = cbsa_data)

#summary(cc_model)

 #tidy(cc_model,  conf.int = TRUE) %>% knitr::kable() 

## Compare models
 anova(cc_model1, cc_model)

######################## Model diagnostics ##############################

 library(performance)

compare_performance(cc_model1, cc_model)

# save model diagnostics plot
png("cclmm_diagnostics.png", width = 14*300, height = 14*300, res = 300)  
check_model(cc_model)

dev.off()

## check distribution of random effects

ranef_vals <- ranef(cc_model)
hist(ranef_vals$cbsa_id[[1]], main="", xlab="Random effect: CBSA")
hist(ranef_vals$state_abb[[1]], main="", xlab="Random effect: State")

##  Model metrics
model_performance(cc_model)


################### create and save report-ready results table ##########

model_tbl <- tbl_regression(
  cc_model,
  intercept = TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  estimate_fun = function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x),
  label = list(pct_white ~ "Percent White in pop",
               pct_pov ~ "Percent pop in pov",
               ruca_agg ~ "Rural-Urban Commuting Area",
               density_log ~ "Log density (people/sq km)")
) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%  modify_header(label ~ "Term") %>%  # rename 'Characteristic' -> 'Term'
  modify_caption("**Cross-Classified Mixed Effects Model for PM2.5**") 


model_tbl

 as_gt(model_tbl) %>%
  gt::gtsave("model_ccmm_results.png")


```

## Approach 3: Multiway cluster adjusted SE (CRSE)
```{r}

# Justifications:
## This computes two-way clustered standard errors:
## Clustered by CBSA
## Clustered by State
## Correcting for overlapping membership

# Limitations
## Does not estimate variance at CBSA or state level.
  ## Cannot ICC: cannot attribute any variation to CBSA or state
## Does NOT add CBSA or state intercepts
## No cluster-level estimates
## Does NOT change coefficient estimates
## Leaves the model as simple OLS.
  ## Only adjusts standard errors
  ## Only adjusts the variance-covariance matrix.
  ## Assumes independence across clusters

cr_model <- feols(
  pm25 ~ pct_white*pct_pov + ruca_agg + density_log,
  data = cbsa_data,
  cluster = ~ cbsa_id + state_abb)

summary(cr_model)

########################### Model diagnostics ##########################

### compare cluster SEs

library(data.table)

coefs <- names(coef(cr_model))

se_table <- data.table(
  term = coefs,
  cluster_cbsa   = sqrt(diag(vcov(cr_model, cluster = ~cbsa_id))),
  cluster_state = sqrt(diag(vcov(cr_model, cluster = ~state_abb))),
  cluster_both = sqrt(diag(vcov(cr_model, cluster = ~cbsa_id + state_abb)))
)

se_table <-  se_table %>% mutate(term = case_when(term == "pct_white" ~ "Percent White in pop",
               term == "pct_pov" ~ "Percent pop in pov",
               term == "ruca_agg" ~ "Rural-Urban Commuting Area",
               term == "density_log" ~ "Log density (people/sq km)",
               term == "pct_white:pct_pov" ~ "White X poverty", TRUE ~ term),
               cluster_cbsa = round(cluster_cbsa, 4),
               cluster_state = round(cluster_state, 4),
               cluster_both = round(cluster_both, 4))

se_table

gt_table <- gt(se_table)

# Save as PNG
gtsave(gt_table, "se_table.png")

## Quick model comparison using AIC and BIC

AIC(cr_model)
BIC(cr_model)
AIC(cc_model)
BIC(cc_model)

################### create and save report-ready results table ##########

cr_tbl <- tbl_regression(
  cr_model,
  intercept= TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  estimate_fun = function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x),
  label = list(pct_white ~ "Percent White in pop",
               pct_pov ~ "Percent pop in pov",
               ruca_agg ~ "Rural-Urban Commuting Area",
               density_log ~ "Log density (people/sq km)"
               )
) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%  modify_header(label ~ "Term") %>%  # rename 'Characteristic' -> 'Term'
  modify_caption("**Multiway cluster adjusted SE Model for PM2.5**") 

as_gt(cr_tbl) %>%
  gt::gtsave("model_crse_results.png")


```

## Approach 4: Generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs)
```{r}

# In GAMs beta coefficients from Linear Regression are replaced with a flexible function (splines) that allows nonlinear relationships 

# Splines allow us to model non-linear relationships for each feature. The sum of many splines forms a GAM.The result is a highly flexible model which still has some of the explainability of a linear regression.

## GAMM Using nlme for multilevel modeling part
cbsa_data$state_cbsa <- interaction(cbsa_data$state_abb, cbsa_data$cbsa_id)

gam_nlm <- gamm(pm25~s(pct_white) + pct_white:pct_pov + pct_pov + ruca_agg + density_log, data= cbsa_data,random = list(state_abb = ~1, state_cbsa = ~1), method = "REML")

########################### Model diagnostics ##########################

## Use these GAMMs to obtain comparison between linear and smooth models (These GAMMS LMM part based on lme4)
smooth_model <- gamm4(pm25~s(pct_white) + pct_white:pct_pov + pct_pov + ruca_agg + density_log, data= cbsa_data,random =~(1|state_abb / cbsa_id))

linear_model <- gamm4(pm25~pct_white + pct_white:pct_pov + pct_pov + ruca_agg + density_log, data= cbsa_data,random =~(1|state_abb / cbsa_id))


anova(linear_model$mer, smooth_model$mer, test="Chisq")

# Plot smooth terms to assess non-linearity of relationship between pm2.5 and pct_white
png("gam_smooth_plot.png", width = 800, height = 600, res = 120)

plot(gam_nlm$gam, shade = TRUE, pages = 1)

# Close device
dev.off()


logLik(gam_nlm$lme)
AIC(gam_nlm$lme)
BIC(gam_nlm$lme)
gam_nlm$lme$sigma
```

```{r}
################### create and save report-ready results table ##########
 ### Fixed effect part

gam_tbl <- tbl_regression(
  gam_nlm$lme,
  intercept= TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  estimate_fun = function(x) sprintf("%.5f", x),
  label = list(`Xs(pct_white)Fx1` ~ "Percent White in pop",
               Xpct_pov ~ "Percent pop in pov",
               Xruca_aggsuburban ~ "Urbanicity - Suburban",
               Xruca_aggurban ~ "Urbanicity - Urban",
               `Xdensity_log` ~ "Log density (people/sq km)",
               `X(Intercept)` ~ "Intercept",
               `Xpct_pov:pct_white` ~ "pct White X pct pov"
               #bc ~ "Black carbon conc",
               #hyads ~ "HyADS"
               #pct_white:pct_pov ~ "White X pov",
               #bc:hyads ~ " Black carbon X HyADS"
               )
) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%  modify_header(label ~ "Term") %>%  # rename 'Characteristic' -> 'Term'
  modify_caption("**Non-linear GAMM for PM2.5**") 

as_gt(gam_tbl) %>%
  gt::gtsave("model_gamm_results.png")

## smooth terms part

smooth_df <- as.data.frame(summary(gam_nlm$gam)$s.table)
smooth_df$term <- rownames(smooth_df)

smooth_df <- smooth_df[, c("term", "edf", "F", "p-value")]
colnames(smooth_df) <- c("term", "edf", "statistic", "p.value")

smooth_df <-  smooth_df %>% mutate(p.value = case_when(p.value==0~"<0.001", TRUE~as.character(p.value)))


smooth_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Smooth Terms") %>%
  gtsave("smooth_terms_gt.png")
```
